token expire.effect: Invalidates token access, immediately by default. Confirm dependent clients have replacement credentials; renewal may not recover an expired token.

token renew.defaults: An omitted extension period is delegated to the broker/client default; the maximum lifetime still bounds renewal.
token renew.effect: Extends bearer-token validity up to its maximum lifetime. Confirm the token identity and credential handling before renewal.

token create.defaults: Token HMAC is redacted unless --show-secrets is supplied. Lifetime bounds are broker-dependent.
token create.effect: Creates bearer credentials. --show-secrets exposes the HMAC; keep it out of logs and screenshots and store it securely.

token list.defaults: No owner filter means all visible tokens. Token HMACs are redacted unless --show-secrets is supplied.

studio.defaults: Starts the local Studio server; install the Studio package alongside the CLI. Bind/port/browser defaults are documented by kafka-studio --help.

cluster unregister-broker.defaults: Unregisters the explicitly named broker; it does not move replicas for you.
cluster unregister-broker.effect: Removes the broker registration; it does not migrate replicas or safely decommission the host by itself. Complete reassignment and verify cluster health first.

cluster info.defaults: Describes the selected cluster; broker ids and addresses depend on its metadata.

cluster update-features.defaults: Upgrade type defaults to upgrade. Use explicit downgrade modes only after checking broker compatibility.
cluster update-features.effect: Changes finalized feature versions. Downgrades may be rejected or unsafe for existing metadata. Confirm the supported feature range and rollback constraints first.

cluster log-dirs.defaults: Queries the requested broker ids; result sizes and partitions are cluster-specific.

cluster raft-voter add.defaults: Use --dry-run to inspect the requested voter and listeners before changing quorum membership.
cluster raft-voter add.effect: Changes the metadata quorum. Verify voter identity/listeners and quorum health; a dry run does not prove the new voter can participate.

cluster quorum.defaults: Reads metadata quorum state; requires a broker supporting the quorum API.

cluster features.defaults: Reads supported/finalized feature metadata; unsupported broker APIs fail explicitly.

cluster reassign execute.defaults: The reassignment file supplies target replicas. --dry-run previews the parsed plan; log_dirs entries are reported as ignored.
cluster reassign execute.effect: Moves partition replicas and can increase network/disk load. Save the current assignment before applying so a deliberate reverse plan can be submitted.

cluster raft-voter remove.defaults: Removes the explicitly named voter; confirmation controls do not establish quorum safety.
cluster raft-voter remove.effect: Changes the voting quorum and can compromise availability if the remaining voters cannot form a majority. Verify quorum health and a recovery plan before confirmation.

cluster reassign list.defaults: Lists active partition reassignments; an empty topics array means none are reported.

cluster elect-leaders.defaults: Uses the requested election type and topic partitions; use --dry-run to inspect the request.
cluster elect-leaders.effect: Changes leadership. Unclean election can lose records unavailable on the elected replica. Inspect ISR health and use a dry run before submitting.

txn terminate.defaults: Uses the optional transaction timeout for the fenced producer; inspect result.errorCode.
txn terminate.effect: Force-terminates an in-flight transaction. Active writers can be fenced or interrupted; inspect result.errorCode and coordinate recovery before restarting them.

txn fence.defaults: No timeout is supplied unless --timeout is set.
txn fence.effect: Invalidates current producer epochs for the selected transactional ids. Active writers can fail and need recovery; coordinate the operation with their owners.

txn abort.defaults: Writes an abort marker for the explicit producer, epoch and topic partition.
txn abort.effect: Writes an abort marker and changes transaction visibility. Confirm producer id/epoch and partition; coordinate with the application recovery procedure.

txn list.defaults: Lists transactions without implicit filters; supplied filters narrow the result.

config set.defaults: Applies the provided key/value entries to the selected resources; use --dry-run for validation.
config set.effect: Changes resource behavior; some broker settings need a restart while dynamic settings apply immediately. Save existing overrides and validate the change before execution.

config list-resources.defaults: Lists supported config resources known to the broker.

config unset.defaults: Removes the named overrides so broker defaults apply; use --dry-run for validation.
config unset.effect: Removes explicit settings and exposes inherited/default values. Record the old overrides before removal so they can be restored.

config describe.defaults: Reads resource configs; it does not change their values.

group delete-offsets.defaults: With no --partition, clears every partition of each selected topic.
group delete-offsets.effect: Removes committed checkpoints. Stop consumers and save current offsets first; their next start may replay or skip records according to reset policy.

group offsets.defaults: Reads committed offsets without committing resolved offsets. With no --topic filter, reads every topic with offsets for this group.

group reset-offsets.defaults: Preview-only unless --execute is present. --topic and --to are required; --to accepts earliest or latest.
group reset-offsets.effect: Stop consumers first. Preview is the default; --execute applies it. Moving backward replays records and moving forward skips records. Save the prior offsets for recovery.

group remove-members.defaults: Removes the specified member identities; consumer membership determines the resulting assignment.
group remove-members.effect: Evicts group members and triggers reassignment. Coordinate with the application to avoid unexpected rebalances and duplicate external side effects.

group list.defaults: Lists consumer groups without an implicit group-id filter.

group describe.defaults: Describes each supplied group id, reporting errors per group.

group delete.defaults: Deletes supplied groups; it does not delete topic records.
group delete.effect: Removes group metadata and committed offsets, not topic records. Stop consumers first; recreating the group may replay or skip records according to reset policy.

admin call.defaults: The selected method determines arguments, return shape, compatibility, and mutation behavior. This is an unstable passthrough. The output example illustrates listTopics; other methods return their own shapes.
admin call.effect: May mutate broker state depending on the method. Inspect admin methods classification and the Admin reference before invoking an unfamiliar method.

admin methods.defaults: Lists the exposed Admin method catalog with classifications; it does not invoke methods.

ping.defaults: Checks the cluster selected by connection resolution; no administrative mutation is performed.

profiles.defaults: Lists all configured profiles and marks the active one; credential fields are redacted.

doctor.defaults: Local configuration diagnostics only. It tolerates config load errors and never tests broker connectivity; use ping for that.

init.defaults: Chooses .ts when the project has tsconfig.json or a TypeScript dependency, otherwise .mjs. Existing files require --force.

completion.defaults: Writes completion for the selected shell; it does not load cluster configuration.

topic offsets.defaults: The selected offset query controls whether the result is a single offset or low/high offsets per partition.

topic add-partitions.defaults: The requested count is the new total, not the number to add. --dry-run validates without changing the topic.
topic add-partitions.effect: Increases the partition count permanently; Kafka does not support shrinking it. Key-to-partition mapping can change. Review ordering assumptions before execution.

topic delete-records.defaults: Requires explicit per-partition offset boundaries; it removes records before those boundaries.
topic delete-records.effect: Deletes records before each supplied offset boundary; this is not an offset reset. Consumers cannot replay the removed records. Save/check the boundaries and data recovery plan first.

topic create.defaults: Explicit replica assignment excludes partition/replication counts. Otherwise flags override cli.topicDefaults, then omitted values follow client/broker defaults. --dry-run validates without creating.
topic create.effect: Creates topics and broker resources. Dry-run validates the request without creation; set explicit partition/replication values for a known cluster.

topic list.defaults: Lists topics without an implicit name filter.

topic describe.defaults: Describes supplied topics; metadata is returned per topic.

topic delete.defaults: Confirmation is required unless --yes or configured confirmation policy permits it. --force overrides internal-topic and batch-size protections.
topic delete.effect: Deletes topics and their records. There is no preview flag or undelete operation. Confirm the cluster and backups before bypassing confirmation with --yes or protections with --force.

topic producers.defaults: With no partition filter, queries every partition of the topic.

share-group offsets.defaults: Reads offsets unless a set/delete operation is requested; without a topic filter, reads the full group state.
share-group offsets.effect: Set/delete operations change future record delivery. Inspect current offsets and coordinate active consumers before mutating; backward changes can redeliver records.

share-group list.defaults: Lists share groups reported by the broker; feature support is broker-gated.

share-group describe.defaults: Describes the supplied share-group ids, reporting errors per group.

share-group delete.defaults: Deletes the selected share groups; topic data is separate.
share-group delete.effect: Removes share-group state. Stop members first and plan how a recreated group should resume delivery.

scram set.defaults: Requires an explicit mechanism and password input. PBKDF2 iterations default to 4096.
scram set.effect: Creates or rotates authentication material. Coordinate client credential rollout to avoid disconnecting users, and retain a secure credential recovery path.

scram list.defaults: With no user names, lists credentials for all users. No password is returned.

scram delete.defaults: Deletes credentials for the selected users/mechanism; other credentials are not a recovery copy.
scram delete.effect: Removes authentication material and can prevent new client connections. Recovery requires provisioning valid credentials again; the old password cannot be read back.

quota alter.defaults: Only supplied set/unset operations are applied; an empty entity name selects a cluster-default entity.
quota alter.effect: Changes client limits and may throttle live applications. Save current quota entries; restore them explicitly if the change affects service health.

quota describe.defaults: Uses the provided entity filters; quota entries and values are broker-specific.

acl remove.defaults: Unspecified resource type, pattern type, operation and permission filters default to any. Principal selection still limits the removal.
acl remove.effect: Revokes matching authorization bindings. Broad any filters can remove multiple permissions. Save the existing bindings before removal so they can be recreated.

acl add.defaults: Pattern type defaults to literal, permission to allow, and host to *. Use --dry-run to inspect entries before applying.
acl add.effect: Changes authorization. A permissive principal/host/pattern can grant broader access than intended. Inspect a dry run; remove the exact added bindings to undo it.

acl list.defaults: Unspecified resource type, pattern type, operation and permission filters default to any.
